questions.contextText: Summary of Passage (Q.24–30): In Greek mythology, the ten-year Trojan War began at the wedding of King Peleus and Thetis. Eris, goddess of discord, was excluded because her presence always sparked quarrels. Seeking revenge, she tossed a golden apple inscribed 'for the most beautiful' into the feast, sparking a dispute among Hera, Athena, and Aphrodite. Prince Paris of Troy was chosen to judge and awarded the apple to Aphrodite, who promised him Helen, the most beautiful woman in the world. Traveling to Sparta, Paris received the hospitality of King Menelaus, but eloped with Helen to Troy, prompting Menelaus to launch the Greek expedition.
questions.questionText: Why did Peleus leave Eris off the wedding guest list?

She did not like any wedding celebration.
